label: Denver Music Venues
description: 25 Front Range stages — from Red Rocks to sweaty basement shows.

items.name: Red Rocks Amphitheatre
items.note: Two 300-foot sandstone monoliths and the best acoustics on Earth. Non-negotiable canon.

items.name: The Bluebird Theater
items.note: A restored 1913 movie house and the beating heart of Colfax live music.

items.name: Mission Ballroom
items.note: The newest big room, with a movable floor so every show fits.

items.name: Larimer Lounge
items.note: Where the band you love now played to 40 people three years ago.

items.name: Hi-Dive
items.note: South Broadway's sweaty little indie institution.

items.name: Globe Hall
items.note: Live music and a smoker out back. What more do you want.

items.name: Levitt Pavilion Denver
items.note: Free outdoor shows all summer. Genuinely.

items.name: Ball Arena
items.note: Where the enormo-tours land. Great if you like your artist as a distant ant.

items.name: Lion's Lair
items.note: A tiny, gloriously grimy Colfax rock dive. You'll leave sticky and happy.

items.name: Skylark Lounge
items.note: Rockabilly, a photo booth, and a pool table upstairs.

items.name: Seventh Circle Music Collective
items.note: Volunteer-run, all-ages, donation-based. The real underground.

items.name: The Grizzly Rose
items.note: A mechanical bull, a giant dance floor, and line dancing you did not consent to.

items.name: Coyote Ugly Denver
items.note: Yes, they dance on the bar. Yes, it is exactly like the movie.

items.name: Stampede
items.note: A country mega-club the size of a small airport.

items.name: Temple Denver
items.note: Bottle service, lasers, and bass you feel in your teeth.
